# Architecture

Crossfoot is one Python package with a command-line entry point, files on disk, and a static results page. No
server, no database server, no queue. Each part below names the requirement in `.prod-build/contract.md` that forces it.

## The idea in one paragraph

A scanned table prints its own totals. If every cell is read into a ledger, each value can be tested twice: its
row has to add up to the total printed at the end of the row, and its column has to add up to the total printed
under the column. One wrong cell fails both sums, and the two failing sums cross at it. Crossfoot reads the scan
with a vision model, accepts a value only when both sums hold, re-reads the cells where they do not, and then uses
the closed ledger to audit a published file that was copied from the same scan.

## Layout of the repository

```
crossfoot/
  cli.py        command-line entry point (argparse): audit, read, verify-known, budget, site
  sources.py    the eight benchmark counties: scan URL, published-file URL, cache under data/ (M1, M4)
  render.py     pdftoppm wrapper: page -> PNG at a dpi; crops with Pillow (M1, M3)
  segment.py    finds blocks and column lines on a ruled page from the image itself (M1)
  model.py      gateway client, JSON parsing with one repair attempt, cost meter, budget guard, rate limit (M7)
  tracing.py    neatlogs setup and span helpers; a no-op when the key is absent (M7)
  layouts/
    matrix.py   precincts as columns, three rows per candidate, totals both ways (Panola)
    report.py   one precinct per page, one row per candidate with its own total (San Saba, Cottle and others)
    profile.py  decides which layout a county uses and tests the decision on the first pages (M1)
  ledger.py     SQLite ledger: cells, printed totals, checks, events; resume (M2, M6)
  checks.py     row sums, column sums, grand totals, grid completeness; pure functions (M2)
  agent.py      the investigation loop: a model chooses the next action for each open item; code enforces the rules (M3)
  audit.py      compares the closed ledger with the published file; classifies and settles disagreements (M4)
  outputs.py    county.json, findings.json, corrected CSV, report.md, the site's data bundle (M5, M8)
  policy.py     the one stored answer and its default (S1)
tests/          unit tests for checks, ledger, audit, budget, resume, agent rules; no network
site/           the static results page (plain HTML, CSS and JS; no build step) (M8)
runs/           one folder per run; small results are committed, caches are not
data/           downloaded scans and files; never committed
```

## Inputs

Eight Texas counties from the OpenElections project's 2024 general election benchmark. All eight scans are
image-only PDFs (no text layer): Cottle 12 pages, Foard 16, Jones 20, Limestone 42, Lynn 37, Panola 6, San Saba 21,
Scurry 38.

- Scan: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-sources-tx/master/2024/general/2024%20<County>%20County%2C%20TX%20precinct-level%20results.pdf`
- Published file: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-data-tx/master/2024/counties/20241105__tx__general__<county>__precinct.csv`
  with columns `county, precinct, office, district, party, candidate, votes, absentee, early_voting, election_day`.

## Two layouts

**Matrix (Panola).** A landscape canvass sheet. The header row lists the precincts as columns and ends in a TOTAL
column. Each candidate is a block: a label at the left, three ruled rows (EARLY, ABSENTEE, PRECINCT), a row of
small printed totals under the columns, and a grand total under the TOTAL column. In the published file EARLY is
`early_voting`, ABSENTEE is `absentee`, PRECINCT is `election_day`, and the small total is `votes`.
Checks per block: for each precinct, early + absentee + precinct = the small total; for each row, the precinct cells
add to the row's TOTAL; the small totals add to the grand total.

**Report (San Saba, Cottle and others).** One precinct per page or section. Each candidate is a row with four
numbers: TOTAL, Absentee, Early Voting, Election Day. Checks per row: total = absentee + early + election day.
Where the page prints a total for the contest, the candidates' totals have to add to it.

`layouts/profile.py` asks the model which layout the first page shows and what the column order is, then reads the
first page under that layout and runs the checks. A profile under which more than a third of the sums fail is
rejected; the other layout is tried; if neither holds the county is reported as "layout not supported" and left alone.

## Reading

1. `render.py` renders a page at 200 dpi.
2. Matrix: `segment.py` finds the blocks as bands of ink separated by blank bands, and the column lines inside a
   block as columns of dark pixels that run the height of the ruled rows. Report: the page is read whole.
3. Matrix: each block is cut into column groups no wider than 1,500 px at 300 dpi, one model call per group; report:
   one page per call. The answer is strict JSON, validated (right number of columns, integers only), with one repair
   request. Every value comes back with the block, row kind and column it belongs to.
4. Which model reads a county is decided by measurement, not fixed. A sample of the first page is read with
   `claude-haiku`; if more than a tenth of the sample's row sums fail, the county is read with `claude-sonnet-4.6`.
   Measured on Panola on 11 October 2026, same code and crops: `claude-haiku` left 85 of 943 printed sums failing
   (44 after a 20-minute re-read loop with 565 more calls); `claude-sonnet-4.6` left 6 of 942.
5. The values go into the ledger as `first_read`, with the page and the pixel box of each value where it is known.

## The ledger (`ledger.py`, SQLite, one file per run)

- `cells(county, page, block_id, contest, candidate, row_kind, column, value, first_read, status, tries, model, x0, y0, x1, y1)`
  with status in `first_read | accepted | failed | cannot_verify`.
- `totals(county, page, block_id, direction, key, value)` for printed row totals, column totals and grand totals.
- `events(ts, county, kind, payload_json)` for everything the agent did, in order. The results page replays these.
- A county is `closed` when every sum holds and the grid has no gap, or every open cell is `cannot_verify`.
- Resume: on start, accepted cells are kept and only open ones are worked on.

## Checks (`checks.py`, no model, no I/O)

Pure functions over the ledger's rows. They return, for each sum, its terms, the printed total, the computed total
and pass or fail, and for each failing cell the sums that cross at it. `locate()` returns the cells that sit on a
failing row sum and a failing column sum at once. Grid completeness lists every precinct, contest and candidate that
is present in one place and absent in another.

## The investigation loop (`agent.py`)

Every value on a matrix sheet sits on two printed sums. A cell sits on its row and its column. The small total under
a column sits on that column and on the grand total (the small totals add to it). A row's printed total sits on its
row and on the grand total (the three row totals add to it). So one wrong value makes exactly two sums fail, and they
cross at it. `checks.locate()` pairs failing sums that share one value and whose differences agree: that value is the
suspect, and the difference says what it would have to be.

The loop works the sums that still fail after the first read, and later every disagreement with the published file.
For a located suspect it looks at the scan again: a re-read of that one value, cut at 400 dpi or more and enlarged.
A value changes only because a re-read of the scan gave the new value; arithmetic says where to look, never what to
write. What pairing cannot locate goes to the model, which is shown the failing sums and what has been tried and
returns one action as JSON:

- `reread {target, dpi, model}`: a single value, a column slice or a row strip
- `conclude {item, verdict, reason}`: `document_inconsistent` or `cannot_verify`
- `ask_policy {question_id}`: use the stored answer, or the default marked as unconfirmed
- `done {item}`

Rules that code enforces whatever the model says: at most six actions per item; re-reads climb one step at a time
(the county's reader, then `claude-sonnet-4.6`, then `claude-opus-4.6`), a step only after the one below has failed
to settle the value; the same target is never re-read twice with the same model and dpi; no value is accepted unless
both of its sums hold; a value the scan shows the same way twice while its two sums still fail is
`document_inconsistent` (the document disagrees with itself there) and the stored policy answer applies; a correction
is written only when the printed totals agree with the new value and disagree with the old one.
Every action and its result is an event in the ledger and a span in neatlogs.

## The audit (`audit.py`)

1. Load the published file. Normalise labels (case, punctuation, party suffixes, running mates).
2. Map the scan's contests and candidates to the file's. Exact and normalised matches first; what is left goes to
   the model once per county as two lists, and code checks that the answer is one-to-one and that mapped pairs have
   close county totals.
3. Compare cell by cell. A disagreement is classified:
   `file_row_fails_own_total`, `wrong_number`, `wrong_column`, `wrong_precinct`, `missing_row`, `extra_row`.
4. Settle it. If the scan's value passes both of its sums and the file's value breaks a printed total, the status is
   `settled_against_file`. If no printed total can decide, `cannot_verify`. If the scan's own totals disagree with
   its cells, `document_inconsistent`, and the stored policy answer applies.
5. Keep the evidence: the crop of the block, the sums with their terms, the old and the new value.
   Every finding carries `confirmed_by_person: false` until a person changes it.

## Outputs (`outputs.py`)

`runs/<run_id>/run.json` (start, end, commit, model calls, tokens, cost, counties), and per county
`county.json` (cells, totals, checks, events), `findings.json`, `crops/*.png`, `corrected/<published file name>`,
`changes.diff` and `report.md`. `crossfoot site build --run <id>` copies what the results page needs into
`site/data/`: `index.json`, one JSON per county, the page images that carry findings (at most 1600 px wide) and the crops.

## Tracing and cost (`tracing.py`, `model.py`)

`neatlogs.init(api_key=..., workflow_name="crossfoot")`; the gateway client is wrapped with `neatlogs.wrap(OpenAI(...))`.
A county run is a `WORKFLOW` span, the loop is an `AGENT` span, each tool is a `TOOL` span
(`@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name=...)`), tagged with run, county, page, block and cell. `neatlogs.flush()` and
`neatlogs.shutdown()` run at exit. The cost meter adds up each response's token usage, and `crossfoot budget` reads
the gateway's own figure for the key (`GET <gateway root>/key/info`, where the root is `LITELLM_BASE_URL` without
`/v1`). The guard refuses a call that would pass the limit.

## The results page (`site/`)

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript modules, no framework and no build step, so it deploys as static files. It reads
`site/data/`. The scan is an image inside a container with CSS perspective; cells, sums and marks are DOM and SVG
elements placed in the image's own coordinates, so they tilt with it and stay real, selectable elements.
`UI-SPEC.md` is the specification.

## What can fail and what happens

| Dependency | Failure | What the program does |
|---|---|---|
| Model gateway | rate limit, timeout | waits and retries once, then marks the item cannot-verify |
| Model gateway | budget reached | stops before the call, writes what it has, exits with a clear message |
| Model answer | not valid JSON, wrong column count | one repair request, then the block is marked failed and goes to the loop |
| Scan or file | cannot be downloaded | that county stops with the URL; other counties continue |
| neatlogs | key missing or unreachable | the run continues untraced and says so on its first line |
| Position finding | no ruled lines | crops fall back to whole blocks and the page shows crops without cell marks |

## Decisions

- SQLite for the ledger, because a stopped run has to resume and the page replays events in order.
- A JSON action protocol for the loop instead of provider tool-calling, so it runs unchanged on any model the gateway serves.
- CSS 3D for the stage instead of WebGL: the sheet is the only object, text has to stay crisp and selectable, and
  the page has to work with the effect off.
"""Row sums, column sums and grid completeness. Pure functions: no I/O, no model.

Inputs are plain dicts as the ledger returns them. A cell needs `page, block_id, row_kind, column, value`
(value None means unread). A printed total is `page, block_id, direction, key, value` with direction
'row' (key = row_kind), 'col' (key = column) or 'grand' (key ignored).
A cell is identified by the tuple (page, block_id, row_kind, column), called a cell key below.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN = "TOTAL"  # a cell in this column is the row's printed total, not a term


@dataclass
class Check:
    kind: str                 # 'row' | 'col' | 'grand'
    page: int
    block_id: str
    key: str                  # row_kind for a row sum, column for a column sum, '' for grand
    terms: list = field(default_factory=list)  # [(cell key, value)]
    printed: int | None = None
    computed: int | None = None  # None when a term is unread
    ok: bool = False


def cell_key(c: dict) -> tuple:
    return (c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"], c["column"])


def _printed(totals, direction):
    return {(t["page"], t["block_id"], t["key"] if direction != "grand" else ""): t["value"]
            for t in totals if t["direction"] == direction}


def _make(kind, page, block, key, cells, printed) -> Check:
    terms = [(cell_key(c), c["value"]) for c in cells]
    computed = None if any(v is None for _, v in terms) else sum(v for _, v in terms)
    return Check(kind, page, block, key, terms, printed, computed, computed is not None and computed == printed)


def row_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """One check per (page, block, row_kind) that has a printed row total: the row's cells must add to it."""
    printed = _printed(totals, "row")
    groups: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        if c["column"] != ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN:
            groups.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"]), []).append(c)
    return [_make("row", *k, g, printed[k]) for k, g in groups.items() if k in printed]


def column_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """One check per (page, block, column) that has a printed column total: the column's cells must add to it."""
    printed = _printed(totals, "col")
    groups: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        groups.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"], c["column"]), []).append(c)
    return [_make("col", *k, g, printed[k]) for k, g in groups.items() if k in printed]


def grand_checks(totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """The printed column totals of a block must add to its printed grand total."""
    grand = _printed(totals, "grand")
    out = []
    for (page, block, _), g in grand.items():
        cols = [t for t in totals if t["direction"] == "col" and t["page"] == page and t["block_id"] == block]
        terms = [((page, block, "col", t["key"]), t["value"]) for t in cols]
        comp = sum(v for _, v in terms)
        out.append(Check("grand", page, block, "", terms, g, comp, comp == g))
    return out


def grid_gaps(cells: list[dict]) -> list[tuple]:
    """Cell keys that are absent or unread where the block's grid says they should be.

    Within a block the grid is every row_kind crossed with every column that appears in it.
    Returns sorted (page, block_id, row_kind, column) tuples.
    """
    blocks: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        b = blocks.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"]), {"rows": set(), "cols": set(), "have": set()})
        b["rows"].add(c["row_kind"]); b["cols"].add(c["column"])
        if c["value"] is not None:
            b["have"].add((c["row_kind"], c["column"]))
    return sorted((p, bid, r, col) for (p, bid), b in blocks.items()
                  for r in b["rows"] for col in b["cols"] if (r, col) not in b["have"])


def locate(rows: list[Check], cols: list[Check]) -> list[tuple]:
    """Cell keys that sit on a failing row sum and on a failing column sum at once."""
    bad_rows = {k for ch in rows if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
    bad_cols = {k for ch in cols if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
    return sorted(bad_rows & bad_cols)


def all_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    return row_checks(cells, totals) + column_checks(cells, totals) + grand_checks(totals)


def crossing(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """For each cell key, the row and column checks it sits on (a cell on no printed sum maps to an empty list)."""
    on: dict = {cell_key(c): [] for c in cells if c["column"] != ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN}
    for ch in row_checks(cells, totals) + column_checks(cells, totals):
        for k, _ in ch.terms:
            on[k].append(ch)
    return on

class BudgetExceeded(Exception):

def price(model: str, prompt_tokens: int, completion_tokens: int) -> float:
    pin, pout = PRICE_PER_MTOK.get(model) or max(PRICE_PER_MTOK.values())
    return (prompt_tokens * pin + completion_tokens * pout) / 1e6


def parse_json(text: str):
    """Parse a model answer as JSON, tolerating a code fence around it. Raises ValueError."""
    t = (text or "").strip()
    m = re.match(r"^```(?:json)?\s*(.*?)\s*```$", t, re.S)
    if m:
        t = m.group(1)
    try:
        return json.loads(t)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"answer is not valid JSON: {e}") from None


def root_url(base: str) -> str:
    base = base.rstrip("/")
    return base[:-3] if base.endswith("/v1") else base


def gateway_spend() -> tuple[float, float | None]:
    """(spend, max_budget) for the key, from the gateway. Reads the key from the environment; never prints it."""
    req = urllib.request.Request(root_url(os.environ["LITELLM_BASE_URL"]) + "/key/info",
                                 headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["LITELLM_API_KEY"]})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
        info = json.load(r)["info"]
    return float(info.get("spend") or 0), (None if info.get("max_budget") is None else float(info["max_budget"]))

    def __init__(self, client=None, *, model=DEFAULT_MODEL, budget=DEFAULT_BUDGET, min_interval=1.1,
                 sleep=time.sleep, retry_wait=5.0, timeout=120):
        if client is None:
            from openai import OpenAI
            from . import tracing
            client = tracing.wrap(OpenAI(base_url=os.environ["LITELLM_BASE_URL"],
                                         api_key=os.environ["LITELLM_API_KEY"], timeout=timeout))
        self.client, self.model, self.budget = client, model, budget
        self.min_interval, self.sleep, self.retry_wait = min_interval, sleep, retry_wait
        self.calls = self.prompt_tokens = self.completion_tokens = 0
        self.cost = 0.0
        self._last = 0.0

    def _guard(self):
        est = self.cost / self.calls if self.calls else FIRST_CALL_ESTIMATE
        if self.cost + est > self.budget:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"run budget ${self.budget:.2f} reached (estimated spend ${self.cost:.4f} after "
                                 f"{self.calls} calls); refusing the next call")

    def _call(self, messages, model):
        self._guard()
        from openai import APIConnectionError, APITimeoutError, RateLimitError
        for attempt in (0, 1):
            wait = self.min_interval - (time.monotonic() - self._last)
            if wait > 0:
                self.sleep(wait)
            self._last = time.monotonic()
            try:
                r = self.client.chat.completions.create(model=model, messages=messages, temperature=0)
                break
            except (RateLimitError, APITimeoutError, APIConnectionError):
                if attempt:
                    raise
                self.sleep(self.retry_wait)
        u = r.usage
        self.calls += 1
        self.prompt_tokens += u.prompt_tokens
        self.completion_tokens += u.completion_tokens
        self.cost += price(model, u.prompt_tokens, u.completion_tokens)
        return r.choices[0].message.content or ""

    def ask_json(self, prompt: str, image=None, *, validate=None, model=None):
        """Ask for JSON. A bad answer (not JSON, or `validate` raises ValueError) gets one repair request."""
        model = model or self.model
        content = [{"type": "text", "text": prompt}]
        if image is not None:
            content.append({"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": data_url(image)}})
        messages = [{"role": "user", "content": content}]
        text = self._call(messages, model)
        for repaired in (False, True):
            try:
                data = parse_json(text)
                if validate:
                    validate(data)
                return data
            except ValueError as e:
                if repaired:
                    raise
                messages = messages + [
                    {"role": "assistant", "content": text},
                    {"role": "user", "content": f"That answer was rejected: {e}. Answer again with only the "
                                                "corrected JSON, nothing else."}]
                text = self._call(messages, model)

from __future__ import annotations

    rc = 0

        try:

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sqlite3
import time
from pathlib import Path

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cells(
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, county TEXT, page INTEGER, block_id TEXT, contest TEXT, candidate TEXT,
  row_kind TEXT, column TEXT, value INTEGER, first_read INTEGER, status TEXT DEFAULT 'first_read',
  tries INTEGER DEFAULT 0, model TEXT, x0 INTEGER, y0 INTEGER, x1 INTEGER, y1 INTEGER, reason TEXT,
  UNIQUE(county, page, block_id, row_kind, column));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS totals(
  county TEXT, page INTEGER, block_id TEXT, direction TEXT, key TEXT, value INTEGER,
  UNIQUE(county, page, block_id, direction, key));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events(
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ts REAL, county TEXT, kind TEXT, payload_json TEXT);
"""
STATUSES = ("first_read", "accepted", "failed", "cannot_verify")


class Ledger:
    """One SQLite file. Cells are keyed by (county, page, block_id, row_kind, column)."""

    def __init__(self, path: str | Path = ":memory:"):
        self.db = sqlite3.connect(str(path))
        self.db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self.db.executescript(SCHEMA)
        if "reason" not in {r["name"] for r in self.db.execute("PRAGMA table_info(cells)")}:
            self.db.execute("ALTER TABLE cells ADD COLUMN reason TEXT")  # ledgers made before the loop existed

    def close(self):
        self.db.close()

    def put_cell(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, value, *, contest=None, candidate=None,
                 model=None, box=(None, None, None, None)):
        """Insert a first read, or re-read an open cell. An accepted cell is never overwritten (resume)."""
        self.db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO cells(county,page,block_id,contest,candidate,row_kind,column,value,first_read,model,x0,y0,x1,y1)"
            " VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)"
            " ON CONFLICT(county,page,block_id,row_kind,column) DO UPDATE SET value=excluded.value,"
            " tries=tries+1, model=excluded.model WHERE status!='accepted'",
            (county, page, block_id, contest, candidate, row_kind, column, value, value, model, *box))
        self.db.commit()

    def set_status(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, status, reason=None):
        if status not in STATUSES:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown status {status!r}")
        self.db.execute("UPDATE cells SET status=?, reason=? WHERE county=? AND page=? AND block_id=? AND row_kind=? "
                        "AND column=?", (status, reason, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column))
        self.db.commit()

    def reread_cell(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, value, model=None):
        """Record one re-read of a cell: tries goes up by one, the value is the one kept, the model only if it changed it."""
        self.db.execute("UPDATE cells SET value=?, tries=tries+1, model=COALESCE(?, model) WHERE county=? AND page=? "
                        "AND block_id=? AND row_kind=? AND column=? AND status!='accepted'",
                        (value, model, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column))
        self.db.commit()

    def put_total(self, county, page, block_id, direction, key, value):
        self.db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO totals VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                        (county, page, block_id, direction, key, value))
        self.db.commit()

    def event(self, county, kind, payload=None):
        self.db.execute("INSERT INTO events(ts,county,kind,payload_json) VALUES(?,?,?,?)",
                        (time.time(), county, kind, json.dumps(payload or {})))
        self.db.commit()

    def cells(self, county=None, status=None) -> list[dict]:
        q, a = "SELECT * FROM cells WHERE 1=1", []
        if county:
            q += " AND county=?"; a.append(county)
        if status:
            q += " AND status=?"; a.append(status)
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q + " ORDER BY id", a)]

    def totals(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
        q, a = "SELECT * FROM totals", []
        if county:
            q += " WHERE county=?"; a.append(county)
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q, a)]

    def events(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
        q, a = "SELECT * FROM events", []
        if county:
            q += " WHERE county=?"; a.append(county)
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q + " ORDER BY id", a)]

    def open_cells(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
        """Cells that still need work: first_read or failed."""
        return [c for c in self.cells(county) if c["status"] in ("first_read", "failed")]

75	def plan_groups(edges, label_x0, total_x1, *, scale, max_w) -> list[Group]:
76	    """Cut the columns (n+1 edges) into runs whose image, with labels in the first and TOTAL in the last, fits max_w."""
77	    n = len(edges) - 1
78	    label_w = (edges[0] - label_x0) * scale
79	    total_w = (total_x1 - edges[n]) * scale
80	    out, c = [], 0
81	    while c < n:
82	        first = c == 0
83	        w = label_w if first else 0.0
84	        c1 = c
85	        while c1 < n:
86	            nw = w + (edges[c1 + 1] - edges[c1]) * scale
87	            last_extra = total_w if c1 + 1 == n else 0.0
88	            if c1 > c and nw + last_extra > max_w:
89	                break
90	            w, c1 = nw, c1 + 1
91	        last = c1 == n
92	        out.append(Group(c, c1, first, last, w + (total_w if last else 0.0)))
93	        c = c1
94	    return out

105	def group_image(hi_png, b, edges, g, scale, dest: Path) -> Path:
106	    """Stitch the strips of one group side by side: labels | columns | TOTAL, all the block's full height."""
107	    y0, y1 = round(b.y0 * scale), round(b.y1 * scale)
108	    xs = [(b.x0, edges[0])] if g.labels else []
109	    xs.append((edges[g.c0], edges[g.c1]))
110	    if g.total:

112	    with Image.open(hi_png) as im:
113	        strips = [im.crop((round(a * scale), y0, round(z * scale), y1)) for a, z in xs]
114	    out = Image.new(strips[0].mode, (sum(s.width for s in strips), y1 - y0), 255)
115	    x = 0
116	    for s in strips:
117	        out.paste(s, (x, 0))
118	        x += s.width

338	    """Boxes of cells, printed totals and blocks of one matrix-layout county, and crops of them from the scan."""

340	    def __init__(self, county, cols, root=None):
341	        from ..sources import DATA
342	        self.county, self.cols, self.root = county, list(cols), root or DATA

344	        self._rule_cache: dict = {}

347	    def _page(self, page):
348	        if page not in self._pages:
349	            blocks = find_blocks(page_png(self.county, page, GEO_DPI, self.root))
350	            self._pages[page] = (blocks, _edges(blocks, len(self.cols)))

353	    def _block(self, page, bid):
354	        blocks, edges = self._page(page)
355	        i = 0 if bid in ("reg", "cast") else int(bid.rsplit("-b", 1)[1])
356	        if i >= len(blocks) or edges is None:
357	            raise GeometryError(f"no column lines found for {bid} on page {page}")
358	        rows = HEADER_ROWS if bid in ("reg", "cast") else ROWS
359	        self._cur_page = page
360	        self._rules(blocks[i], edges)
361	        return blocks[i], edges, rows

363	    def _rules(self, b, edges):
364	        """y of each horizontal rule across the precinct columns inside the block's ruled height, found in the image."""
365	        key = (b.y0, b.x0)
366	        if key not in self._rule_cache:
367	            import numpy as np
368	            png = page_png(self.county, self._cur_page, GEO_DPI, self.root)
369	            with Image.open(png) as im:
370	                g = np.asarray(im.convert("L"))[b.rule_y0 - 3:b.rule_y1 + 4, edges[0]:edges[-2]]
371	            cover = (g < 110).mean(axis=1) >= 0.6
372	            ys = []
373	            for s_, e_ in segment._runs(cover):
374	                ys.append(b.rule_y0 - 3 + (s_ + e_) // 2)
375	            self._rule_cache[key] = ys
376	        return self._rule_cache[key]
377	
378	    def _row(self, b, rows, kind):
379	        i = rows.index(kind)
380	        ys = self._rule_cache.get((b.y0, b.x0)) or []
381	        h = (b.rule_y1 - b.rule_y0) / len(rows)
382	
383	        def edge(j):    # an even split, moved onto a drawn rule when one lies within 5 px
384	            y = b.rule_y0 + j * h
385	            near = min(ys, key=lambda r: abs(r - y), default=None)
386	            return round(near if near is not None and abs(near - y) <= 5 else y)
387	        return edge(i), edge(i + 1)

389	    def block_box(self, page, bid):
390	        try:
391	            return self._block(page, bid)[0].box
392	        except GeometryError:
393	            return None

395	    def cell_box(self, page, bid, row, col):
396	        b, edges, rows = self._block(page, bid)
397	        y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, row)
398	        ci = self.cols.index(col)
399	        return (edges[ci], y0, edges[ci + 1], y1)
400	
401	    def total_box(self, page, bid, direction, key):
402	        try:
403	            b, edges, rows = self._block(page, bid)
404	            n = len(self.cols)
405	            if direction == "row":
406	                y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, key)
407	                return (edges[n], y0, b.x1, y1)
408	            if bid == "reg":
409	                return None
410	            if direction == "col":
411	                ci = self.cols.index(key)
412	                if bid == "cast":
413	                    y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, "SMALL")
414	                    return (edges[ci], y0, edges[ci + 1], y1)
415	                return (edges[ci], b.rule_y1, edges[ci + 1], min(b.y1, b.rule_y1 + SMALL_ROW))
416	            if bid == "cast":
417	                y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, "SMALL")
418	                return (edges[n], y0, b.x1, b.y1)
419	            return (edges[n], b.rule_y1, b.x1, b.y1)
420	        except (GeometryError, ValueError):
421	            return None

423	    def target_box(self, page, bid, t):
424	        """The box of a re-read target, without padding."""
425	        b, edges, rows = self._block(page, bid)
426	        kind = t["kind"]
427	        if kind == "cell":
428	            return self.cell_box(page, bid, t["row"], t["column"])
429	        if kind == "column":
430	            ci = self.cols.index(t["column"])
431	            y0 = self._row(b, rows, "EARLY")[0]
432	            if bid == "cast":
433	                return (edges[ci], y0, edges[ci + 1], self._row(b, rows, "SMALL")[1])
434	            return (edges[ci], y0, edges[ci + 1], min(b.y1, b.rule_y1 + SMALL_ROW))
435	        if kind == "row_total":
436	            return self.total_box(page, bid, "row", t["row"])
437	        if kind == "col_total":
438	            return self.total_box(page, bid, "col", t["column"])
439	        if kind == "grand":
440	            return self.total_box(page, bid, "grand", "")
441	        raise GeometryError(f"unknown target kind {kind!r}")

443	    def crop(self, page, bid, t, dpi, dest: Path):
444	        """Cut the target out of the page at `dpi`, with padding, enlarged so its digits are at least 40 px tall.
445	        Returns (path, box at 200 dpi)."""
446	        try:
447	            box = self.target_box(page, bid, t)
448	        except ValueError:
449	            box = None
450	        if box is None:
451	            raise GeometryError(f"cannot place {t} in {bid} on page {page}")
452	        k = dpi / GEO_DPI
453	        x0, y0, x1, y1 = box
454	        with Image.open(page_png(self.county, page, dpi, self.root)) as im:
455	            win = (max(0, round((x0 - PAD) * k)), max(0, round((y0 - PAD) * k)),
456	                   min(im.width, round((x1 + PAD) * k)), min(im.height, round((y1 + PAD) * k)))
457	            c = im.crop(win)
458	        s = scale_for(dpi, t["kind"])
459	        if s > 1:
460	            c = c.resize((round(c.width * s), round(c.height * s)), Image.LANCZOS)
461	        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
462	        c.save(dest)
463	        return dest, box

ROWS = ("EARLY", "ABSENTEE", "PRECINCT")
GOOD = {"1": (10, 2, 3), "2": (20, 4, 6)}     # column -> EARLY, ABSENTEE, PRECINCT
HAIKU, SONNET = "claude-haiku", "claude-sonnet-4.6"


def make_block(led, page, bid, good=GOOD, wrong=None, row_totals=None, col_totals=None, grand=None):
    """A block whose printed totals are those of `good`; `wrong` maps (row, column) -> the value the first read gave."""
    wrong = wrong or {}
    for col, vals in good.items():
        for r, v in zip(ROWS, vals):
            led.put_cell("x", page, bid, r, col, wrong.get((r, col), v), contest="C", candidate=f"cand {bid}")
        led.put_total("x", page, bid, "col", col, (col_totals or {}).get(col, sum(vals)))
    for i, r in enumerate(ROWS):
        led.put_total("x", page, bid, "row", r, (row_totals or {}).get(r, sum(v[i] for v in good.values())))
    led.put_total("x", page, bid, "grand", "", grand if grand is not None else sum(sum(v) for v in good.values()))


class FakeGeo:
    def __init__(self):
        self.targets = []

    def crop(self, page, bid, target, dpi, dest):
        self.targets.append((bid, dict(target), dpi))
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        Image.new("L", (10, 10), 255).save(dest)
        return dest, (0, 0, 10, 10)

    def total_box(self, page, bid, direction, key):
        return None

    def block_box(self, page, bid):
        return None


class FakeGw:
    """Decisions come from `decide(prompt, n)`, re-reads from `read(target, model, n)`. Logs every call."""
    def __init__(self, geo, decide, read, model=HAIKU):
        self.geo, self.decide, self.read, self.model = geo, decide, read, model
        self.calls = self.prompt_tokens = self.completion_tokens = 0
        self.cost = 0.0
        self.log = []

    def ask_json(self, prompt, image=None, *, validate=None, model=None):
        self.calls += 1
        model = model or self.model
        if image is None:
            ans = self.decide(prompt, sum(1 for m, k, _ in self.log if k == "decide"))
            self.log.append((model, "decide", prompt))
        else:
            bid, target, dpi = self.geo.targets[-1]
            ans = self.read(bid, target, model, sum(1 for m, k, _ in self.log if k == "read"))
            self.log.append((model, "read", (bid, target, dpi)))
        if validate:
            validate(ans)
        return ans

        if t["kind"] == "cell":

    def strip_crops(self, page, bid, row, dpi, dest, per):
        self.targets.append((bid, {"kind": "row_strip", "row": row}, dpi))
        cols = list(GOOD)
        out = []
        for i in range(0, len(cols), per):
            p = dest.with_name(f"{dest.stem}-s{i}.png")
            p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            Image.new("L", (10, 10), 255).save(p)
            out.append((p, cols[i:i + per], (0, 0, 10, 10)))
        return out


class Reader:
    """Answers re-reads: `says(target, model)` gives the value (or a list for a strip)."""
    def __init__(self, says):
        self.says, self.asked = says, []

    def __call__(self, bid, t, model, n):
        self.asked.append((t["kind"], model))
        v = self.says(t, model)
        if t["kind"] == "row_strip":
            return {"values": v}
        return {"value": v}


def go(led, says, decide=None, geo=None, **kw):
    geo = geo or StripGeo()
    rd = Reader(says)

        return rd(bid, t, model, n)
    gw = FakeGw(geo, decide or (lambda p, n: pytest.fail("the model was asked to decide")), read)
